newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN FRIDAY TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN FRIDAY TRADE.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed in a busy liquid market on Friday.

Dealers forecast a market surplus of Z$100 million for the end of the day, saying the central Reserve Bank had offered for auction treasury bills worth Z$700 million to discount houses which only took up paper worth Z$600 million at 24.69 percent.
The bills were being sold on the secondary market at 24.55 percent, versus 24.65 percent overnight.

NCDs maturing after 30 days were being bought at 26.5 percent from 26 percent and sold at 25 percent, slightly down on Thursday's 25.75 percent while those with maturity of 60 and 90 days were being bought at 26.5 percent but sold at 25.5 percent.
Bankers' acceptance bills were quoted at 25.25 percent (buying) and 24.55 percent (selling) compared to 25.75 percent (buying) and 24.75 percent on the selling side previously.
The call rate edged up to 23.5 percent from 22 percent.
